name: LHS 288

candidates.name: LHS 288 b (unnamed astrometric candidate)
candidates.note: 2007 astrometric study suggested a possible ~2.4 Jupiter-mass companion, but the authors could not rule out an undetected faint star; never confirmed and not in the NASA Exoplanet Archive.

notes: Distance from Gaia DR3 parallax 206.97 mas (SIMBAD) = 15.76 ly; your 15.70 is within tolerance. Mass 0.1085+/-0.0091 Msun (CARMENES-based value cited on Wikipedia). SIMBAD spectral type M5.5V; Wikipedia gives M5V. Age not constrained.

name: GJ 1002
notes: Planets from Suarez Mascareno et al. 2023 (RV, ESPRESSO+CARMENES); both non-transiting, both in the habitable zone. Radii unknown (Archive lists ~1.03/1.10 Re but these are 'Calculated Value' from a mass-radius relation, so set null). Distance from Gaia DR3 parallax 206.35 mas. Age not well constrained.

name: Gliese 412
position_corrections: Distance corrected 15.80 -> 16.00 ly (Gaia DR3 parallax: A 203.89 mas = 16.00 ly; B/WX UMa 203.83 mas = 16.00 ly). RA/Dec fine.
notes: No planet claims found; RV monitoring of A showed no significant planet-induced variation and speckle imaging found no companion at 1-10 AU. B is a UV Ceti-type flare star. Age 3 Gyr is a single cited estimate on Wikipedia; treat as approximate. Separation A-B ~28 arcsec (B at RA 11.0919 h, Dec +43.522).

name: Groombridge 1618

candidates.name: Groombridge 1618 (122-day RV signal)
candidates.note: Marcy & Benitz 1989 reported a 122-day periodicity interpretable as a >=4 Jupiter-mass planet; possibly due to stellar activity, never confirmed. A 2010 MMT imaging search found no companion. Herschel found evidence of a cold debris disk.

notes: Also GJ 380. Distance from Gaia DR3 parallax 205.31 mas = 15.89 ly. Mass 0.670+/-0.033 Msun. SIMBAD spectral type K6VeFe-1 vs Wikipedia K7.5Ve. Age 6.6 Gyr is a single estimate.

name: AD Leonis

candidates.name: AD Leonis b
candidates.note: Tuomi et al. 2018 proposed a 2.23-day RV signal (~0.24 Jupiter masses min.) matching the stellar rotation period. Studies from 2020 onward attributed it to stellar activity; a 2022 study ruled out planets >27 Earth masses at the rotation period. Not in NASA Exoplanet Archive confirmed table.

notes: Young, very active flare star. Distance from Gaia DR3 parallax 201.41 mas = 16.19 ly. SIMBAD lists spectral type dM3; Wikipedia M3.5eV.

name: Gliese 832

candidates.name: Gliese 832 c
candidates.note: Announced 2014 as a habitable-zone super-Earth; Gorrini et al. 2022 showed the RV signal behaves like stellar activity. Not in the NASA Exoplanet Archive confirmed table.

notes: GJ 832 b values are the Archive default (Philipot et al. 2023, RV+astrometry), giving a TRUE mass of ~0.99 Jupiter masses (314.65 Me). Other solutions: An et al. 2025 330 Me, a=3.651 AU; older RV-only minimum masses ~200-216 Me. Radius is only an Archive 'Calculated Value', so null. Age: Wikipedia 6+/-1.5 Gyr; Philipot 2023 8.1 Gyr - range given. Spectral type: SIMBAD M1.5V, Wikipedia M2V. Distance from Gaia DR3 parallax 201.33 mas.

name: 40 Eridani

candidates.name: 40 Eridani b (HD 26965 b, 'Vulcan')
candidates.note: Proposed in 2018 as a ~42-day super-Earth. Burrows et al. 2024 ('The death of Vulcan', NEID) found the RV signal is rotationally modulated stellar activity. Not in the NASA Exoplanet Archive confirmed table.

notes: Distance from Gaia DR3 parallax of A, 199.61 mas = 16.34 ly (your 16.30 within tolerance). Age of A is poorly constrained (6.9+/-4.7 Gyr), so null; B's white-dwarf cooling age is ~1.8 Gyr (not total system age). B's spectral type: Wikipedia DA4, SIMBAD DA2.9. B mass 0.558+/-0.012 per Wikipedia (older literature ~0.573).

name: 70 Ophiuchi

candidates.name: 70 Oph historical companion claims
candidates.note: 19th/20th-century astrometric claims (Jacob and See in the 1800s; 1932 and 1943 proposals) were shown to be erroneous. Modern RV searches find no planets; Saturn-mass-or-smaller habitable-zone planets around A not excluded.

notes: Distance: Gaia DR3 gives 16.68 ly (A, 195.57 mas) and 16.65 ly (B, 195.86 mas); Hipparcos (van Leeuwen 2007) gives 16.58 ly. Used 16.66 (mean of Gaia components); your 16.6 within tolerance. Age estimates disagree: ~2.8-3.0 Gyr (per-component fits) vs 6.2+/-1.0 Gyr; range given.

name: Altair
notes: Distance from Hipparcos (van Leeuwen 2007) parallax 194.95 mas = 16.73 ly. Age 88+/-10 Myr (Rieutord et al. 2024, cited on Wikipedia). Rapid rotator (oblate). Visual companions WDS B-G are optical, not physically associated. No planet claims.

name: Sun
notes: Planet values from NASA NSSDC fact sheets: semi-major axis, mass and radius are ratios to Earth (radius = equatorial diameter ratio); periods in days from the main fact sheet. Fact sheet lists Earth's period as 365.2 d. NSSDC Sun fact sheet gives no age; 4.6 Gyr (meteoritic ~4.57 Gyr) from Wikipedia. RA/Dec null for the Sun.
